facts.fact: UNICEF reports that the Ntlafatsa Bana project's digital birth registration system registers births on tablets, with birth certificates handed over at its launch in Ha Tankele, Qhoasing Community Council; deaths are not mentioned (no launch date given; the article's date is used).

UNICEF says the system has replaced slow manual processes with real-time tablet-based registration, operated by trained village health workers and civil registration officers and integrated with the NISSA social assistance database; it does not name the register the record is held in (the article's date is used).

systems.owner: Equitable Lesotho - Ntlafatsa Bana project, a joint initiative of the Government of Lesotho, the European Union and UNICEF
systems.tiers: community level, by village health workers and civil registration officers; launched at Ha Tankele, Qhoasing Community Council
the birth registration system is integrated with the national social assistance database

note: No count of councils or offices using the system, and no statement of who funds or owns it beyond the joint initiative.
